proof_nl: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer with m <= x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. Therefore m + 1 is an integer strictly larger than m, so it cannot also satisfy m + 1 <= x; hence x < m + 1. Combining these inequalities gives m <= x < m + 1. Subtracting m throughout yields 0 <= x - m < 1. In particular, x - floor(x) < 1. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
